concepts.name: 北欧家居
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one polished, production-quality desktop homepage design concept for POLY LAB, a Chinese interior renovation and spatial design web app. Landscape image, approximately 1536x1024, straight-on full UI screenshot, edge-to-edge page, no laptop frame, no perspective mockup, no browser chrome, no watermark. Must feel designed by an excellent brand/product design studio with deliberate typography, impeccable alignment, usable navigation and attractive interior imagery. Chinese is primary, with small tasteful English editorial labels. Clearly legible actual simplified Chinese UI text. Preserve product identity POLY LAB and the three core tasks: 仓库 (furniture and materials collection), 空间重建 (define an empty room with walls, door and window), 自由设计 (arrange furniture and render interiors). Navigation text: 首页 / 仓库 / 空间重建 / 自由设计, plus 服务设置. Use headline exactly “让理想的空间，从这里发生。” and subtitle “准备喜欢的物件，画出家的轮廓。剩下的，一起设计。” Core imagery must differentiate real cutout furniture, empty architectural room shell with no furniture, and warm fully furnished interior render. Keep blue as brand primary, yellow as accent; no green theme. Do not use tilted italic Chinese type or a generic SaaS gradient. Show one complete concept only, not a collage of alternatives. Art direction A: optimistic Scandinavian home brand with bold electric IKEA-inspired cobalt blue #0058A3, sunshine yellow #FFDB00, warm ivory. Lively high-end home catalog meets useful design app. White slim header with confident bold POLY LAB wordmark. Hero left half has large beautiful rounded geometric extra-bold upright Chinese headline arranged into two strong lines, comfortable generous whitespace, small cobalt capsule “从一间房开始”, blue primary call to action “开始设计” with small yellow arrow. Hero right half features a beautifully lit large cutaway dollhouse empty room floating directly on cream canvas, pale oak floor, white walls, simple door, one large window, no furniture inside; beside it a few thoughtful furniture cutouts on blue/yellow circular shapes. Below the hero, show the three workflows as three compact horizontal visual tiles with crisp typography, large 01 02 03, thin blue borders, minimal shadow, and explicit task names; each tile has corresponding small realistic imagery. Asymmetric editorial balance, reassuring and welcoming, tastefully rounded corners, ample yet economical spacing, distinctive typography and functional clear hierarchy. Yellow used sparingly for highlights rather than excessive large surfaces. This must be a substantially new and visually appealing design, not three oversized pale grey identical cards.

Art direction B: sophisticated architectural atelier / Swiss editorial design system. An elegant 72px vertical blue project rail on left with minimal white line icons; main header carries POLY LAB, slim nav, services and a small outlined “新建空间” button. Central typography is exceptionally beautiful upright Chinese modern neo-grotesk with restrained weights and dark blue clean condensed English small labels, not calligraphic. A calm two-line headline upper left, a tiny “SPACE / MATERIAL / LIFE” index upper right. Each column has title and short function line at bottom and restrained arrow controls. Add a thin bottom strip “最近的空间” with two compact project rows and tiny floorplan thumbnails, no complex stats. Strong horizontal baseline alignment, airy composition, very subtle graph-paper detail only near room drawing. Tastefully refined designer tool, exceptionally crisp, organized and confident. Blue dominant in typography and linework, lots of white, yellow as precision accent. Clearly different from a consumer retail website.

Integrate an opaque deep cobalt-blue editorial text panel over the left third of this hero (not gradient), with large masterfully typeset ivory upright Chinese headline and small spaced English label “MAKE ROOM FOR LIFE”. Yellow rectangular call-to-action “开始自由设计” with navy arrow. Photography remains dominant on right two thirds. Tiny yellow corner accents and thin navy rules. Strong premium editorial typography, restrained deep blue and yellow, warm photographic textures, mostly square or slightly softened corners, no floating big grey cards, no glassmorphism. Show enough genuine app controls to feel like useful personal design platform rather than only advertisement. Make the composition luxurious yet approachable, coherent and visually memorable.
